title: DNA methylome signatures of prenatal exposure to synthetic glucocorticoids in hippocampus and peripheral whole blood of female guinea pigs in early life.
ehr_evidence: DNA from the hippocampus and whole blood of each animal was extracted using AllPrep Mini Kit and QIAamp DNA Mini Kit; RRBS libraries were then generated and sequenced on a NextSeq500 (no electronic/computerised individual-level health records were used).
summary: A controlled animal study of prenatal synthetic glucocorticoid (betamethasone) versus saline exposure in female guinea pigs, comparing genome-wide DNA methylation in hippocampus and whole blood at postnatal day 14.
key_findings: In the hippocampus 7004 differentially methylated CpG sites (DMCs) were identified (79.9% hypermethylated, 20.3% hypomethylated) and in blood 16,740 DMCs (62.7% hypermethylated, 37.3% hypomethylated) in response to sGC exposure.
1044 DMCs were localized to the same CpG sites in both tissues, representing 14.9% of hippocampal and 6.2% of blood DMCs.

A positive correlation was found between methylation difference percent in hippocampus and blood across 1044 common DMCs (R = 0.31, n = 1044, P < .0001), with over 90% showing the same directionality of change.
134 genes showed differential methylation in both tissues and 61 genes showed DMCs at identical CpG sites in both tissues.
No enrichment of glucocorticoid regulatory elements (GREs) was observed around differentially methylated CpG sites in either tissue.
captured_features: Genome-wide DNA methylation at single-nucleotide (CpG) resolution via reduced representation bisulfite sequencing (RRBS)
Differentially methylated CpG sites (DMCs) and differentially methylated regions (DMRs)
Gene pathway enrichment (Gene Ontology biological process, FDR < 0.05)
DNA motif and transcription factor binding site enrichment (MEME, JASPAR)
Spearman correlations of methylation difference percent between hippocampus and blood
study_design: Controlled experimental animal study (prenatal treatment vs saline control, female offspring only)
population: Hartley-strain female guinea pigs; maternal treatment in late gestation (GD 40/41, 50/51, 60/61); offspring examined at postnatal day 14 (n = 6/treatment/tissue)
limitations: Animal model (guinea pig) limits direct human extrapolation
Only female offspring examined, so male effects unknown
Majority of DMCs were tissue-specific, limiting blood as a universal brain biomarker
Motif analysis was in silico and found no GRE enrichment
data_availability_statement: The data discussed in this publication have been deposited in NCBI's Gene Expression Omnibus 48 and are accessible through GEO Series accession number GSE163447.
